findings.title: Audit Cost Liability
findings.fact: If, as a result of any such audit, Administrative Fees are determined to have been underpaid by more than five percent (5%) for the period audited, Contractor shall pay the costs of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.
findings.business_implication: Bidders face significant financial penalties for underpayment of administrative fees exceeding 5%, including audit costs or treble damages.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure accurate sales reporting and administrative fee payments to avoid penalties.

findings.title: Potential Conflict in Order of Precedence
findings.fact: The RFQ states that the resulting Agreement is comprised of documents with a specified order of precedence in which the Agreement Terms and Conditions come first and the RFQ is last, while Section 1 of the RFQ states that the RFQ incorporates the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and additional terms set forth in the RFQ, its Attachments, and Appendices. This creates potential ambiguity as to which terms control if the RFQ and its attachments conflict with the Agreement Terms and Conditions.
findings.business_implication: Bidders should be aware that although the order of precedence lists the Agreement Terms and Conditions first, the RFQ also incorporates additional terms; conflicting provisions may require clarification during the procurement or contract administration.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the order of precedence carefully and seek clarification from OGS if any conflicts arise between the RFQ/attachments and the Agreement Terms and Conditions before submitting a response.

findings.title: Delivery Extension Approval Process
findings.fact: The RFQ allows Authorized Users to request extensions beyond 60 calendar days, subject to OGS approval, but also limits approval for substantially delayed deliveries to industry-wide events or acceptable extenuating circumstances, creating ambiguity regarding OGS's discretion and the conditions for approving extensions beyond 60 days.
findings.business_implication: There is ambiguity regarding the scope of OGS's authority to approve extensions beyond 60 days and the conditions under which such approvals will be granted, potentially leading to disputes.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from OGS on the process for extensions beyond 60 days and the criteria for approval.

quotes.quote: If an Authorized User wants to extend the delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days, the Authorized User may submit a written request to extend the Product delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days to OGS for its approval.

Approval of substantially delayed deliveries (over 60 calendar days), when the delayed delivery will impact more than one order fulfillment in a thirty (30) day time frame for more than 75 calendar days per incident, will be limited to delays that are a result of an industry wide event or other acceptable extenuating circumstance, that limits or prohibits Contractor’s ability to deliver within Agreement delivery timeframes.
